_note: Human-written explanations for Practice Exam 11, keyed by question number. Merged into exam-11.json by parse-exams.mjs at build time, so edits here survive rebuilds. Add more exams as explanations/exam-N.json.
1: AWS shifts capital expenditure (CapEx — building data centers upfront) to operational expenditure (OpEx — pay-as-you-go), removing large initial ownership costs.
2: Classroom Training (live virtual or in-person courses) and Online Tech Talks (live educational webinars with interactive Q&A) are AWS's instructor-led education options.
3: Access to the AWS Management Console is front-facing web traffic. Enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and strict password policies directly protects these logins.
4: Subnets and Security Groups are core networking constructs managed directly within the Amazon VPC interface.
5: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, AWS is solely responsible for the physical security of data centers, infrastructure hardware, and the virtualization layer.
6: Consolidated billing groups multiple sub-accounts onto one invoice and treats aggregate usage as a single total, qualifying you faster for volume-tiered pricing discounts.
7: With managed services (like Amazon RDS), AWS handles routine tasks such as patching the underlying OS/database engine and managing automatic backups.
8: AWS Regions are independent. To expand into a new Region you simply point your tools/scripts there and start deploying — no new contract is required.
9: Elastic Load Balancers automatically distribute incoming traffic across multiple targets and are designed to handle constantly changing network traffic patterns.
10: The Business Support Plan is the lowest tier offering 24/7 technical support by phone and chat, plus a target response time of under 1 hour for production system impairments.
11: Amazon S3 provides highly durable storage with millisecond retrieval. Glacier classes require longer retrieval, so standard S3 is the right answer for immediate online access.
12: AWS Professional Services is a global team of experts offering paid engagements that help enterprises accelerate their cloud migration journey.
13: The Business Support Plan is the minimum tier with 24/7 phone/chat support and a sub-1-hour response target for production issues.
14: AWS Config continuously monitors and records your resource configurations, letting you audit configuration history and evaluate changes for compliance.
15: AWS Trusted Advisor checks your configurations against best-practice pillars and returns actionable findings, including under-utilized resources (cost) and loose permissions (security).
16: Amazon RDS is the managed service for hosting relational SQL engines like MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Oracle.
17: Programmatic calls via the AWS CLI require an Access Key ID and a Secret Access Key tied to an IAM user.
18: Data protection, configuring encryption (at rest and in transit), and managing access keys are the customer's responsibility under the shared model.
19: Amazon EFS provides a simple, serverless, elastic NFS file share optimized for Linux workloads.
20: Interactive sign-ins use a username/password; programmatic actions (SDKs, CLI) use the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key pair.
21: Shared controls are handled by both parties. Awareness & Training fits: AWS trains its staff, and you must train your own employees on security.
22: Instance Store volumes live on disks physically attached to the host and are ephemeral — data is lost if the instance stops, hibernates, or terminates.
23: Consolidated billing combines usage across accounts onto one invoice, helping you reach volume discount tiers faster.
24: Step Functions (orchestration), DynamoDB (NoSQL), and SNS (pub/sub) are all serverless — no servers to provision or scale.
25: Dedicated Hosts allocate isolated physical servers entirely to you — meeting compliance needs for physical isolation and enabling bring-your-own-license (per-socket/per-core).
26: Granting least-privilege permissions gives users only the access they need, and MFA protects privileged admin accounts from compromise.
27: AWS CloudFormation lets you model, provision, and manage your entire environment using declarative code templates (YAML/JSON).
28: Availability Zones are isolated locations within a Region. Deploying across multiple AZs ensures high availability — if one AZ fails, the others handle traffic.
29: Amazon Aurora is a fully managed MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible database built for the cloud that scales storage automatically (up to 128 TB).
30: Loose coupling is a core design principle: components are independent, so one failing doesn't cascade across the whole system.
31: The Concierge Support team is exclusive to the Enterprise Support plan — it provides billing and account assistance. Trusted Advisor and support cases are available on other plans too, so they aren't Enterprise-only.
32: Moving to the cloud shifts spending from upfront capital expense (CapEx — buying and owning hardware/data centers) to variable operational expense (OpEx — pay-as-you-go for what you use).
33: Dedicated Hosts give you isolated physical servers, satisfying compliance isolation requirements and supporting bring-your-own-license.
42: AWS Basic Support (free) includes only documentation, whitepapers, and the AWS Discussion Forums / re:Post community. Technical Account Managers and direct engineer support require paid plans (Business/Enterprise).
34: Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes are designed for low-cost archival of backups that don't need millisecond access.
35: The Business Support Plan is the minimum tier with 24/7 phone/chat support and a sub-1-hour response target for production issues.
36: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off, but they can be interrupted with a 2-minute warning.
37: Amazon S3 stores large raw video assets, while Amazon CloudFront caches and delivers that content from edge locations worldwide for low-latency streaming.
38: Edge locations (via Amazon CloudFront) bring content closer to users and cache static data, reducing load on your origin servers.
39: The AWS TCO Calculator (now part of the AWS Pricing Calculator / Migration Evaluator) models on-premises vs cloud costs side by side to estimate savings before migrating.
40: The AWS Personal Health Dashboard (now part of the AWS Health Dashboard) alerts you about events affecting your specific resources, unlike the broad Service Health view.
41: By offloading physical infrastructure management to AWS, a business stops spending on running data centers and can focus on its core activities.
43: If a disaster impacts an entire Region, deploying your application across multiple AWS Regions is the way to achieve geographic disaster recovery.
44: AWS secures the underlying storage hardware, but configuring and scheduling backups of your volumes (e.g., EBS snapshots) is your responsibility.
45: Because Spot Instances are interruptible, they are ideal for non-production, flexible background and batch-processing jobs.
46: Latency (proximity to users) and compliance (data sovereignty laws requiring data to stay in specific countries) are primary factors when choosing a Region.
47: The AWS Personal Health Dashboard gives personalized alerts about events impacting your specific resources, unlike the broad Service Health Dashboard.
48: Multi-site active-active runs traffic across multiple fully functional sites at once, giving near-zero RTO/RPO compared to warm standby or pilot light.
49: AWS CodeCommit is a fully managed, secure source-control service that hosts private Git repositories.
50: As in Q3, enforcing MFA and strong password policies are the fundamental ways to secure interactive identity logins.
